newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower on U.S. election result.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower on U.S. election result.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower on Wednesday, reflecting the U.S. dollar's gains in Tokyo after U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election and the Republicans' apparent retention of control of Congress, dealers said.
The local dollar ended at T$27.523 to the U.S. dollar, against Tuesday's T$27.501 close, off a T$27.543 low. Turnover through dealers was an active US$247.5 million.
"The Taiwan dollar's fall was normal, it just reacted to the U.S. dollar rise overseas on U.S. election results," said one Taipei dealer.
Another dealer said the Taiwan dollar's slide "reflected confidence in the U.S. economy after its political uncertainties came to an end" with the conclusion of the election campaign.
"But overall, the (election) results have been well expected. The market is simply showing a celebration rally for the U.S. dollar," he said.
The Taiwan dollar could test support at T$27.55 on Thursday if the U.S. dollar overseas continues to rise, dealers said.
